section_summary: This section chiefly documents U.S. and military processing of applications for entry into occupied Japan, especially commercial travel by American, Burmese, Iranian, European, and Chinese applicants. It also contains Argentine requests to facilitate Japanese emigration from Okinawa and elsewhere to Argentina, which the State Department deferred pending clarification of Argentine representation in Japan. Related papers address passport documentation, protecting-power channels, extensions of military clearance, and proposed residence or family visits.

subfiles.title: Action slip for Thomas Ellis Carr’s travel to Okinawa
subfiles.from: J. D. Scott, Military Permit Branch
subfiles.about: Reports no military objection to Carr’s Okinawa travel and gives arrival instructions.
subfiles.summary: Carr must report immediately to the G-2 headquarters upon arrival; Hong Kong is to be notified.

subfiles.title: English translation of Argentine Embassy note D.E. No. 547
subfiles.to: George C. Marshall, Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests facilities for Okinawan Japanese citizens authorized to immigrate to Argentina.
subfiles.summary: Argentina requests assistance for the Tokashiki, Shinzato, and Nakazato family groups to leave Okinawa.

subfiles.title: Argentine Embassy note D.E. No. 547
subfiles.to: George C. Marshall, Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Spanish original requesting departure facilities for Japanese immigrants.
subfiles.summary: Spanish original of the request concerning the Tokashiki, Shinzato, and Nakazato groups.

subfiles.title: Letter enclosing military permit No. 9225 for Enrico D’Elia
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Department of State
subfiles.about: Transmits D’Elia’s military permit for September travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Permit No. 9225 is valid for one return journey during September 1948.

subfiles.title: Enrico D’Elia application to visit Japan
subfiles.about: Requests commercial travel to Japan to buy merchandise and follow earlier orders.
subfiles.summary: D’Elia proposes visiting Kobe, Osaka, Tokyo, and Yokohama for about two months to purchase pearls, coral, and stones.

subfiles.title: Letter enclosing military permit No. 9226 for Max Salama
subfiles.about: Transmits Salama’s military permit for September travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Permit No. 9226 authorizes one return journey during September 1948.

subfiles.title: Max Salama application to visit Japan
subfiles.about: Requests permission for Salama to buy and process Japanese textiles for overseas export.
subfiles.summary: Salama proposes a three-month visit to Tokyo, Osaka, and Kobe to purchase grey piece goods for export markets.

subfiles.title: Operations memorandum forwarding the Plottegg family application
subfiles.about: Forwards Paul Wolff von Plottegg’s request for permanent residence in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Vienna forwards Plottegg’s letter and security certificates for Department consideration.

subfiles.title: Security certificate for Annemarie Wolff Plottegg
subfiles.about: Certifies that Annemarie Wolff Plottegg was not registered with the Nazi Party.
subfiles.summary: The Murau detachment finds no NSDAP or affiliated-organization membership.

subfiles.title: Paul Wolff von Plottegg application for residence in Kobe
subfiles.to: U.S. Military Government, U.S.F.A., Travel Bureau, Vienna
subfiles.about: Seeks permanent entry with his family to manage his brother’s Kobe factory.
subfiles.summary: Plottegg says his brother Herbert emigrated to the United States and wants him to assume management of the Kobe manufacturing plant. He supplies family details, housing arrangements, financial guarantees, and political-security certificates.

subfiles.title: Letter enclosing military permit for Joseph Ingster
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Department of State
subfiles.about: Transmits Joseph Ingster’s September military permit for Japan.
subfiles.summary: The firm must return the permit if Ingster cannot travel during September 1948.

subfiles.title: Conversation memorandum concerning Dr. Acock’s permit
subfiles.from: L. S. Mellor, Department of State
subfiles.about: Records notification that Dr. Acock’s Japan and Korea permit had arrived.
subfiles.summary: Patricia Albers asks that Shanghai be notified because Acock intends to await clearance there.

subfiles.title: Telegram notifying Shanghai of Adrian M. Acock’s clearance
subfiles.about: Communicates Acock’s military clearance for Japan and Korea.
subfiles.summary: Acock may enter both countries, carry professional effects, and use reimbursable occupation facilities.

subfiles.title: Airgram A-107 on documenting travelers cleared for Japan
subfiles.about: Explains passport endorsements and certified telegram copies for persons cleared to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Department says a brief English passport statement normally suffices, supplemented by application copies. Certified clearance telegrams remain acceptable, while applications from represented foreign nationals should ordinarily pass through their foreign ministries and Washington embassies.

subfiles.title: English translation of Argentine Embassy note D.E. No. 584
subfiles.to: George C. Marshall, Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests departure facilities for the Kishimoto family and Aico Miyagi.
subfiles.summary: Argentina asks assistance for four Japanese citizens holding Argentine landing permits.

subfiles.title: Argentine Embassy note D.E. No. 584
subfiles.to: George C. Marshall, Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Spanish original requesting facilities for Japanese emigrants to Argentina.
subfiles.summary: Spanish original concerning the Kishimoto family and Aico Miyagi.

subfiles.title: State Department reply concerning three Argentine emigration requests
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Argentine requests but postpones action pending clarification of representation in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Department lists the Japanese citizens covered by notes of July 31, August 10, and August 13. It defers action until Argentina clarifies how its interests are represented in occupied Japan.

subfiles.title: State Department note returning Burmese travel applications
subfiles.about: Directs that U Thein and U Hla Thwin apply through British protecting-power channels.
subfiles.summary: Because the United Kingdom protects Burmese interests in Japan, the applications must reach SCAP through British channels. The submitted forms are returned.

subfiles.title: Burmese Embassy note forwarding applications
subfiles.about: Forwards applications by U Thein and U Hla Thwin to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Burma requests prompt transmission of the duplicate applications to the military authorities.

subfiles.title: Burma Foreign Office letter to its Washington embassy
subfiles.from: Tha Din for the Permanent Secretary, Burma Foreign Office
subfiles.about: Requests U.S. permission for U Thein and U Hla Thwin to visit Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Foreign Office forwards company papers after advice reportedly received from the American Embassy in Rangoon.

subfiles.title: Maung Thein Brothers letter to Burma’s Foreign Ministry
subfiles.to: Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Burma
subfiles.about: Asks the ministry to forward its Japan application to Washington.
subfiles.summary: The firm cites procedural advice received from the American Embassy in Rangoon.

subfiles.title: Maung Thein Brothers request for a Japan trade mission
subfiles.about: Requests permission for U Thein and U Hla Thwin to conduct trade talks in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The delegates seek to renew relations with Nichimen Jitsugyo and explore future commodity exchanges.

subfiles.title: U Hla Thwin application for a Japan trade mission
subfiles.about: Applies to accompany U Thein as personal secretary during business talks.
subfiles.summary: Hla Thwin proposes a fortnight in Osaka and Tokyo, entering through Iwakuni.

subfiles.title: U Thein application for a Japan trade mission
subfiles.about: Applies for a fortnight of commercial negotiations in Osaka and Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: U Thein seeks trade agreements covering Burmese produce and Japanese manufactured goods.

subfiles.title: Burma Chamber testimonial for U Thein
subfiles.from: Burma Chamber of Commerce and Industry
subfiles.about: Endorses U Thein’s proposed commercial mission to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The chamber describes U Thein as a reputable rice merchant whose mission could benefit Burmese trade.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Burma Foreign Office letter
subfiles.from: Tha Din for the Permanent Secretary, Burma Foreign Office
subfiles.about: Duplicate forwarding papers for the U Thein and U Hla Thwin applications.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the Foreign Office request reproduced on page 107.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Maung Thein Brothers letter to Burma’s Foreign Ministry
subfiles.to: Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Burma
subfiles.about: Duplicate request to forward the firm’s Japan application to Washington.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the company letter reproduced on page 108.

subfiles.title: Duplicate request for a Maung Thein Brothers trade mission
subfiles.about: Duplicate request for U Thein and U Hla Thwin to visit Japan.
subfiles.summary: Describes proposed negotiations with Nichimen Jitsugyo and possible sightseeing in Japan.

subfiles.title: Duplicate U Thein trade-mission application
subfiles.about: Duplicate application for commercial negotiations in Osaka and Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: U Thein proposes a fortnight of talks on Burmese exports and Japanese imports.

subfiles.title: Duplicate U Hla Thwin trade-mission application
subfiles.about: Duplicate application to accompany U Thein as personal secretary.
subfiles.summary: Hla Thwin plans a fortnight in Osaka and Tokyo via Iwakuni.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Burma Chamber testimonial for U Thein
subfiles.from: Aung Thu, Burma Chamber of Commerce and Industry
subfiles.about: Duplicate endorsement of U Thein’s proposed mission to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The chamber recommends assistance for the prominent Rangoon rice merchant.

subfiles.title: Singapore airgram requesting entry for Annelise Erle
subfiles.about: Requests Japan entry for Annelise Erle during a brief visit to her father.
subfiles.summary: Erle plans to visit Paul Elm in Tokyo while accompanying her returning-resident mother, then depart from Yokohama for Singapore.

subfiles.title: Airgram A-97 explaining the Burmese protecting-power procedure
subfiles.about: Explains why the Burmese applications must proceed through British channels.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy is advised that third-power-protected nationals must normally apply through the protecting power.

subfiles.title: Memorandum for the files on Argentine representation in Japan
subfiles.about: Records policy to postpone Argentine emigration requests until representation is clarified.
subfiles.summary: All similar Argentine requests are to remain pending until Argentina explains its representation in Japan.

subfiles.title: English translation of Argentine Embassy note D.E. No. 591
subfiles.to: George C. Marshall, Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Requests departure facilities for Fumiaki Nakasone and Julio Nakasato’s family.
subfiles.summary: Argentina reports landing permits for Nakasone and Nakasato and asks that they be allowed to leave Japan.

subfiles.title: Argentine Embassy note D.E. No. 591
subfiles.to: George C. Marshall, Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Spanish original concerning Nakasone and the Nakasato-Shinzato family.
subfiles.summary: Spanish original requesting facilities for six Japanese citizens to travel to Argentina.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Argentine note D.E. No. 591
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the request but continues postponement pending clarification of Argentine representation.
subfiles.summary: The Department identifies the six intended emigrants and recalls its August 26 decision. No action will occur until Argentina clarifies representation of its interests in Japan.

subfiles.title: Letter enclosing Erling D. Naess’s military permit
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Department of State
subfiles.about: Transmits Naess’s permit for travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The permit is valid for entry between August 18 and September 18, 1948.

subfiles.title: Erling D. Naess application to visit Japan
subfiles.about: Requests travel for tanker-contract discussions with Japanese shipyards.
subfiles.summary: Naess proposes four weeks in Yokohama and Tokyo to confer about tanker construction contracts subject to SCAP approval.

subfiles.title: Conversation memorandum on permits for Skulstad and Naess
subfiles.from: L. S. Mellor, Department of State
subfiles.about: Records notification that permits for Skulstad and Naess had arrived.
subfiles.summary: Both men may enter Japan from August 18 through September 18 for sixty-day stays.

subfiles.title: Kurth O. Skulstad application to visit Japan
subfiles.about: Requests travel for tanker-construction negotiations in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Skulstad proposes four weeks in Yokohama and Tokyo to consult shipping representatives about Japanese tanker contracts.

subfiles.title: Letter enclosing Kurth O. Skulstad’s military permit
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Department of State
subfiles.about: Transmits Skulstad’s permit for travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The permit is valid for entry between August 18 and September 18, 1948.

subfiles.title: Tehran despatch No. 233 concerning Hossein Afsharieh
subfiles.from: Randall S. Williams, American Embassy, Tehran
subfiles.about: Submits Afsharieh’s renewed Japan trade application with later requested entry dates.
subfiles.summary: Afsharieh rejected earlier clearances and now seeks entry in October, November, or December to buy textiles, yarn, tea, and other goods.

subfiles.title: Army memorandum extending Hossein Afsharieh’s clearance
subfiles.from: J. D. Scott, Military Permit Branch
subfiles.about: Confirms Afsharieh’s extended clearance for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Afsharieh is cleared for sixty days, with entry from October 1 through November 1, 1948.

subfiles.title: Telegram notifying Tehran of Afsharieh’s clearance
subfiles.about: Reports permission for Hossein Afsharieh to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Afsharieh may enter during October for a sixty-day stay and must carry two passport photographs.

subfiles.title: Letter requesting renewed clearance for Hossein Afsharieh
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Department of State
subfiles.to: J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Requests new October–December entry dates for Afsharieh.
subfiles.summary: The Department asks SCAP to reconsider Afsharieh’s unchanged application after he failed to use two earlier clearances.

subfiles.title: Conversation memorandum concerning Fred Kaunitz’s clearance
subfiles.from: L. S. Mellor, Department of State
subfiles.about: Records notification of Kaunitz’s September clearance and arrangements to cable Singapore.
subfiles.summary: Miss Miller directs that Kaunitz be notified in Singapore and documented by the American consulate.

subfiles.title: Army clearance memorandum for Ho Shun Ying and Fred Kaunitz
subfiles.from: Military Permit Branch, Civil Affairs Division
subfiles.about: Confirms Japan entry clearances for Ying and Kaunitz.
subfiles.summary: Ying receives August–September clearance; Kaunitz receives September clearance, each for sixty days.

subfiles.title: File note concerning Fred Kaunitz
subfiles.about: Notes Kaunitz’s substitution as representative and the Singapore notification instructions.
subfiles.summary: Kaunitz replaces a previously approved representative; new forms are being prepared.

subfiles.title: Fred Kaunitz application to visit Japan
subfiles.about: Requests commercial travel to arrange dress manufacturing and purchase Japanese goods.
subfiles.summary: Kaunitz proposes visiting Tokyo, Yokohama, Kobe, Osaka, and possibly other cities to establish manufacturing and export connections.

subfiles.title: Telegram notifying Singapore of Fred Kaunitz’s clearance
subfiles.about: Communicates Kaunitz’s September permission to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Kaunitz may remain sixty days and should receive a certified copy of the telegram.

subfiles.title: Tehran despatch No. 231 concerning Mohamad Ebrahim Javadi
subfiles.from: Randall S. Williams, American Embassy, Tehran
subfiles.about: Submits Javadi’s Japan trade application for SCAP consideration.
subfiles.summary: Javadi seeks November or December entry to purchase textiles and tea after previously importing Japanese goods through India.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Tehran despatch concerning Mohamad Ebrahim Javadi
subfiles.from: Randall S. Williams, American Embassy, Tehran
subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of Javadi’s Japan trade application.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate describing Javadi’s intended purchases, passport, language ability, and forthcoming trade-directory report.

subfiles.title: Telegram granting Mohamad Ebrahim Javadi entry to Japan
subfiles.about: Reports Javadi’s military clearance for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Javadi may enter November 10–December 10 for sixty days and must carry two photographs.

subfiles.title: Letter requesting clearance for Mohamad Ebrahim Javadi
subfiles.to: J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Requests submission of Javadi’s trade application to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: The Department summarizes Javadi’s interest in Japanese textiles and tea and asks the Army to obtain SCAP’s decision. A memorandum, rather than a formal permit, will suffice if approved.

subfiles.title: Army clearance memorandum for Burt Nieburg
subfiles.from: Military Permit Branch, Civil Affairs Division
subfiles.about: Confirms Burt Nieburg’s permission to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Nieburg is cleared for a fifteen-day stay, entering October 15–November 15, 1948.

subfiles.title: Conversation memorandum concerning Ho Shun Ying
subfiles.from: L. S. Mellor, Department of State
subfiles.about: Records notification of Ying’s Japan clearance and authorization to cable Hong Kong.
subfiles.summary: Captain Chu approves notifying Ying through the Hong Kong consulate so she can obtain travel documentation.

subfiles.title: Largely illegible military-clearance memorandum
subfiles.from: Military Permit Branch, Civil Affairs Division
subfiles.about: A clearance form referring to the Commerce letter of July 30, 1948.
subfiles.summary: Most applicant, location, entry-period, and firm fields are illegible or blank in the OCR.

subfiles.title: Ho Shun Ying application to visit Japan
subfiles.about: Requests Japan entry for Ying to work as secretary in the company’s Tokyo branch.
subfiles.summary: Ying would handle Japanese, English, and Chinese correspondence during a sixty-day visit covering Tokyo, Yokohama, Kobe, and Osaka.

subfiles.title: Telegram notifying Hong Kong of Ho Shun Ying’s clearance
subfiles.about: Communicates Ying’s August–September permission to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: Ying may remain sixty days and should receive a certified copy of the telegram.

subfiles.title: Letter requesting clearance for Ahmad Alizadeh
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Department of State
subfiles.to: J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Requests SCAP consideration of Alizadeh’s commercial travel application.
subfiles.summary: Alizadeh seeks prompt travel to buy textiles, chinaware, and glassware for the Kasra Trading Company.

subfiles.title: Army memorandum clearing four commercial travelers
subfiles.from: J. D. Scott, Military Permit Branch
subfiles.about: Lists Japan clearances for four Iranian- and Manila-based travelers.
subfiles.summary: Clearances cover Taghi Pour Dehnad, Ahmad Alizadeh, James Marsden Barnes, and Lionel D. da Silva.

subfiles.title: Tehran despatch No. 232 concerning Ahmad Alizadeh
subfiles.from: Randall S. Williams, American Embassy, Tehran
subfiles.about: Submits Alizadeh’s commercial travel application for SCAP consideration.
subfiles.summary: Alizadeh seeks early entry as a Kasra Trading Company representative interested in textiles, chinaware, and glassware.

subfiles.title: Telegram granting Ahmad Alizadeh entry to Japan
subfiles.about: Reports Alizadeh’s military clearance for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Alizadeh may enter September 10–November 10 for sixty days and must carry two photographs.

subfiles.title: Letter requesting Japan entry for Annelise Erle
subfiles.from: Walter F. Chappell, Department of State
subfiles.to: J. D. Scott, Military Permit Section
subfiles.about: Requests SCAP consideration of Annelise Erle’s short family visit to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Erle plans to arrive at Kobe, visit her father in Tokyo, and depart from Yokohama for Singapore four days later. She will accompany her mother, Tove Elm, a returning Japan resident.

subfiles.title: Telegram granting Taghi Pour Dehnad entry to Japan
subfiles.about: Reports Pour Dehnad’s military clearance for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Pour Dehnad may enter October 10–December 10 for sixty days and must carry two photographs.
